question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts — P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

The invention of the telescope changed astronomy.

P: Scientists could observe distant galaxies.

Q: They discovered stars not visible to the naked eye.

R: Earlier, knowledge was limited to nearby celestial bodies.

S: The new tool opened a whole new universe.

6. Astronomy became a precise science.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph begins with the invention of the telescope, which revolutionized astronomy.
 
• **Sentence R comes first** as it highlights the earlier state of knowledge:
 
 
• "Earlier, knowledge was limited to nearby celestial bodies."
 
 
 
• **Sentence P follows** as it explains how the telescope allowed scientists to observe distant galaxies:
 
 
• "Scientists could observe distant galaxies."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S comes next** as it emphasizes the transformative impact of the new tool:
 
 
• "The new tool opened a whole new universe."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q concludes** by mentioning the discovery of stars not visible to the naked eye:
 
 
• "They discovered stars not visible to the naked eye."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **RPSQ**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Earlier, knowledge was limited to nearby celestial bodies. Scientists could observe distant galaxies. The new tool opened a whole new universe. They discovered stars not visible to the naked eye."
